statement: Sealed, committed and pushed before either arm is asked anything. Both arms run once, on this machine, through a frozen copy of the cockpit's local route. Published whichever way it lands.
question: When Kar's own misses are folded into a playbook he reads before answering, does his direct line repeat those kinds of mistake less on work it has not seen?

loop.misses: every wrong answer Kar's direct line gave, with his brain, in the sealed runs so far (watch.mjs missesOf over the brain's first measurement, with the brain; the fix pass, the brain as first switched on; the fix pass, the fixed brain)
loop.shapes: each miss read for its shape (watch.mjs shapeOf): tool-detour (went looking instead of reading the brain), wrong-number (a neighbouring number), half-pair (one of two asked), wrong-name (a neighbouring build, commit or name), no-answer
loop.playbook: one rule per shape that has happened, ordered by count, with the latest real misses as examples (watch.mjs playbook); a shape not seen for three runs is retired; after every run the loop folds the new misses and writes the next version

call.route: si-didy/kar-cockpit.watch-measure.mjs route("local", [question], hasImages=false, hasFiles=true) — the fix pass's frozen route plus three changes, all the same for both arms: the system prompt read from a pinned file, greedy decoding (temperature 0, seed 7), and an 8k window
call.system: Kar's persona and live state (the brain as of the seal, morning line, shares, asks, lesson shapes) snapshotted once at the seal to ~/.si-didy/brain/watch/system.txt — kept on this machine because it carries his sandbox lines; pinned by its sha256
call.model: qwen2.5:7b through Ollama on this machine

arms.withLoop: the same, with playbook v1 appended

call.order: without first, then with, each as its own process
call.ask: each question alone, no history, followed by: Answer in one short line.
call.graded: brain.mjs gradeAnswer: the reply matches the question's pattern, case-insensitive; a wrong reply's shape by watch.mjs shapeOf

In the fix pass, how many of the 30 questions did the brain as first switched on get right?

rules.rule: with the playbook, at least 2 fewer wrong answers of a shape it learned than without
with the playbook, at least as many answers right as without
every question answered right without the playbook is answered right with it
after the run, the loop folds the held-out misses into playbook v2, and the live direct line carries v2

disclosures: The 20 held-out questions were written after playbook v1 and are deliberately of the shapes Kar's misses took — that is what a repeat mistake is. They were never used to build the playbook, and no held-out question appears in it.
The playbook's rule wording was written by Kar once, per shape; which rules appear, in what order and with which examples is decided by the loop from the misses alone.

Greedy decoding and a pinned prompt make both arms deterministic up to the playbook text, but one run of 20 questions on one 7B is a small test: a difference of one or two answers can be noise in what the extra text does to the model.
The fix pass ran with the default window, which may have cut long tool turns; this test gives both arms an 8k window.

predictions.said: before either arm was asked anything, by Kar
predictions.fewer-repeats: unsure — the misses were mostly a neighbouring number on a crowded line; a rule plus two real examples should help a 7B a little, and two fewer is a real bar on 20 questions
predictions.no-regression: fail, likely — adding 2,000 characters changes greedy outputs everywhere, and one answer that flips from right to wrong fails this
